To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(i) the notion of goal dropping and adoption can be defined and analyzed in a general manner and (ii) the implementation of dropping and adoption is based on a number of different motivations that lead to different mechanisms for dropping and adoption.

(1) dropping and adoption of declarative goals is a fundamental aspect of the dynamics of declarative goals, (2) dropping and adoption can be motivated by a variety of reasons, (3) dropping and adoption mechanisms can be implemented based on these motivations, (4) the mechanisms are related to their motivations, and (5) the mechanisms are implemented in the programming language 3APL.

1) the notion of goal dropping and adoption in agent programming has not been sufficiently formalized; 2) the goal dynamics can be analyzed by identifying motivations for goal dropping and adoption; 3) the goal dynamics are related to the notion of belief update in logic programming; and 4) the goal dynamics depend on the notion of goal satisfaction and the way it is implemented in an agent programming language.
